stem:
Ira builds a 2-stage snack code: first she picks one of 4 chutneys, then one of 3 breads. Every chutney–bread pair is allowed.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: There are only 3 codes, because the bread count alone is the total.
The total number of codes is $4\times3=12$, the product of the choices at each stage.
Equal choice counts across stages can be written with powers; here the stages differ, so the product $4\times3$ is the right form.
Any meal price list is also counted by this same $4\times3$ product.

teacher.key_rationale: Multi-stage codes multiply the per-stage choices: 4 then 3 gives 12. Using only the bread count drops a stage. Stretching the same product onto unrelated price lists over-extends the rule.
